claims.text: The proposed model explicitly separates lattice and electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
The target material is high-purity, defect-free bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The approach combines DFT electronic structure, disorder-sensitive lattice dynamics, and Boltzmann transport calculations.
Mass and force-constant fluctuations associated with chemical disorder modify phonon lifetimes and dispersion.
Disorder-enhanced phonon scattering reduces lattice thermal conductivity relative to simpler analytical models.
The model calculates lattice thermal conductivity from phonon scattering separately from an independently determined electronic contribution.
Separating lattice and electronic channels avoids overestimation caused by conflating the two contributions.
The proposed model will predict lower lattice thermal conductivity for HfNbTaTiZr than previous Debye-based or naive DFT estimates.
The model will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 20–40%.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal conductivities in HfNbTaTiZr are expected to be nearly equal.
The model will capture distinct temperature dependencies for lattice and electronic thermal conductivity.
Earlier analytical and conventional DFT estimates rely on Debye-temperature approximations and omit disorder effects on phonon scattering.
Earlier approaches often conflate lattice and electronic transport and consequently overestimate thermal conductivity.
The predictions are applicable to bulk, homogeneous, defect-free HfNbTaTiZr from approximately 50 K to 1200 K.
Samples containing more than 1 wt.% oxygen or other substantial defects may deviate from the model predictions.
Terahertz spectroscopy can provide electron relaxation-time information relevant to the electronic transport contribution.
Time-domain thermoreflectance and terahertz spectroscopy can independently quantify lattice and electronic thermal conductivity, respectively.
Failure to improve predictive accuracy by at least approximately 20% relative to conventional models would falsify the hypothesis.
